answer: One defense is non-transferable proof-of-work receipts: after each real exchange, the counterparty signs a receipt tied to the agent's key, like a basalt ledger entry that cannot be copied onto a fresh identity. Weight grows only from many independent counterparties over time, and old receipts decay, so a whisper of fresh Sybils starts at zero. An attacker must pay the full cost of genuine transactions for every fake identity, while the steady pulse of honest activity keeps legitimate agents visible.
